chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Will you specialise me with a supplication?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: O One, O Glorified, O Unique, O Eternal, O He who did not beget and was not begotten, and there was none comparable to Him. O Mighty, O Generous, O Affectionate, O Bestower, O Hearer of supplications, O Most Generous of those asked, and O Best of those who give. O Allah, O Allah, O Allah.' I said, 'And Nuh (Noah) certainly called upon Us, so excellent are the Responders.'

Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'Yes, excellent is the Responder, excellent is the One supplicated to, and excellent is the One asked from'.

'I ask You by the Light of Your Face, and I ask You by Your Might, and Your Power, and Your Compulsion, and I ask You by Your Kingdom, and Your Fortified Shield, and by Your Grip, and all Your Pillars, and by the right of Muhammad, and by the right of the Successors after Muhammad, that You should send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You should do such and such with me.'

key_terms.لَمْ يَلِدْ وَ لَمْ يُولَدْ: He did not beget and was not begotten

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for fulfilling needs according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* presents a concise yet profound supplication (*du'a*) emphasizing Allah's absolute uniqueness (*Tawhid*) through the recitation of key divine names, linking the Prophet's tradition with Imam al-Sadiq's teaching. It uniquely incorporates the Quranic verse of Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:3) to affirm God's indivisibility, while concluding with a petition grounded in the intercessory rights (*Haqq*) of the Prophet and the Imams, reflecting the Shia emphasis on their spiritual authority. The reference to Prophet Nuh highlights the efficacy of calling upon Allah as the ultimate Respondent, reinforcing the theme of divine accessibility in times of need.
